newsitem.title: USA: NYCE cotton futures called to open down 0.10 cent.
newsitem.headline: NYCE cotton futures called to open down 0.10 cent.

text.p: NYCE cotton futures were called to open 0.10 cent per lb lower on Thursday based on market orders at 1017 EDT, dealers said.
The U.S. Department of Agriculture put net sales for the week ended August 7 at 104,300 bales in the 1997/98 crop. Shipments totaled 107,200 bales.
Both USDA numbers were in line with analysts' expectations.
Despite the strong data, prices could ease today on technicals. Nearby support was pegged at a gap on the charts between 74.26 cents and 74.10 cents.
"The locals went home long so we could be down on technicals irrespective of exports," Sharon Johnson, an analyst with Frank Schneider and Co Inc, said.
Wednesday, most-active December cotton ended up 0.11 cent at 74.89 cents a lb, having ranged from 74.95 to 74.50 cents. The rest of the board closed 0.10 higher to 0.13 cent lower.
Volume remained light at an estimated 7,500 lots.
